evidence_requirements.statement: Landing observes and binds target T0, combines sealed candidate C with T0 into an isolated integration tree I, and records an integration-specific EvidencePlan.
Candidate receipts are reused only when their subjects and assumptions remain valid; invalidated and integration-sensitive verifiers run against I.
LandingAttestation binds T0, CandidateAttestation C, I, intent digest, integration receipts, policy/runtime profile, and expected landing mechanism.
Integration uses compare-and-swap target protection, marks drift stale, reconstructs and reverifies, and rejects conflicting or behavior-breaking integration.
Authorized merge, squash, and rebase strategies are accepted only when exact resulting-state equivalence is established; candidate refs and CandidateAttestation semantics remain compatible.
After integration, actual landed state is independently checked against the LandingAttestation before LANDED completion and anchor are recorded.
Control-plane documentation reports attestation/proof boundaries accurately and does not claim proof of correctness beyond recorded evidence.

non_goals: Do not claim proof of correctness; attest only to properties established by exact evidence.
Do not change CandidateAttestation semantics or remove existing candidate refs.
Do not perform remote integration, push, release, deployment, or other external effects.
Do not manually edit kernel-owned receipts, attestations, events, grants, or generated views.
objective: Close candidate-to-landed TOCTOU gap with explicit landing transaction

requirements.statement: Landing observes and binds target T0, combines sealed candidate C with T0 in an isolated synthetic integration workspace, produces exact integration tree I, and derives an integration-specific EvidencePlan.
Candidate EvidenceReceipts are reused only when their subjects and assumptions remain valid; invalidated and integration-sensitive verifiers run against I.
LandingAttestation binds T0, CandidateAttestation C, I, intent digest, integration receipts, policy/runtime profile, and expected landing mechanism.
Integration uses compare-and-swap target protection, marks target drift stale, reconstructs and reverifies, and rejects conflicting or behavior-breaking integration.

Authorized merge, squash, and rebase strategies are accepted only when exact resulting-state equivalence is established, while existing candidate refs and CandidateAttestation semantics remain compatible.
After integration, the actual landed state is independently checked against the LandingAttestation before LANDED completion and anchor are recorded.
Durable control-plane documentation distinguishes candidate and landing attestation from proof of correctness and records the explicit transaction boundary.

consequences: This changes the authority boundary between sealed candidates and landed state for every future integration.
Incorrect tree or evidence binding could record a false landed completion or reject a valid integration.
risk.review: Review the transaction state machine, compare-and-swap behavior, synthetic integration isolation, receipt subject validity, strategy equivalence, conflict handling, stale-attestation recovery, and landed-tree mismatch rejection. Verify that legacy candidate refs and CandidateAttestation fields remain unchanged and that documentation distinguishes attestation from proof of correctness.
